definitions.explanation: A traditional toy consisting of two long poles with footrests, used for walking at an elevated height. Made from bamboo in traditional Japanese style.

examples.japanese: {竹馬|たけうま}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}れる→乗る：00511_noru⟧⟦よう→よう：01114_you⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: I learned how to walk on stilts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{運動会|うんどうかい}→運動会：03013_undoukai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{竹馬|たけうま}⟦{競走|きょうそう}→競走：15644_kyousou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We had a stilt race at the sports day.

examples.japanese: {竹馬|たけうま}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{友|とも}→友：03466_tomo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{幼|おさな}なじみ→幼馴染：12429_osananajimi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: 'Takeuma no tomo' refers to a childhood friend.

notes:
LITERAL MEANING:
・⟦{竹|たけ}→竹：02220_take⟧ (bamboo) + ⟦{馬|うま}→馬：01865_uma⟧ (horse) = "bamboo horse"
・Traditionally made from bamboo poles
・Modern versions often made from aluminum or plastic

IDIOMS:
・{竹馬|たけうま}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{友|とも}→友：03466_tomo⟧ (childhood friend, lit. "stilt friend")
  → Friends from a young age who played together on stilts

TRADITIONAL GAME:
・Popular children's activity in Japan
・Often used at ⟦{運動会|うんどうかい}→運動会：03013_undoukai⟧ (school sports festivals)
・Requires balance and practice
